fields: Without answer choices, what is the best architecture response to this scenario? A routine classifier passes all quality thresholds on a faster model while a stronger model costs much more. What is the best choice?
Use the faster model for that workload unless other constraints justify the stronger model. Model choice is a workload-specific trade-off, not a prestige decision.
Resolve this production scenario for Claude model selection: A model is being retired. What should the team do before switching to its replacement?
Run task-specific regression, safety, latency, and cost evaluation. Model migration can change behavior and should be evaluated.
What should an architect recommend in this Claude model selection situation? A workflow has easy classification cases and rare complex exceptions. What design may improve economics if validated?
Route routine cases to a fast model and difficult cases to a stronger model. Evaluated routing can match model capability to workload difficulty.
State the preferred architecture action for this design-review scenario: Which evidence is strongest for choosing between two Claude models for a production task?
Results on a representative eval suite for that task plus latency/cost measurements. Architecture should use representative workload evidence.

Resolve this production scenario for prompt engineering techniques: A straightforward extraction task already meets its quality target zero-shot. What should the team do?
Keep the simpler prompt unless evaluation identifies a failure. Use the lightest technique that passes the evaluation.
What should an architect recommend in this prompt engineering techniques situation? A long prompt mixes policy, examples, retrieved text, and user data. What improvement is most direct?
Structure the prompt so trusted instructions, examples, context, and inputs are clearly separated. Clear structure reduces ambiguity about the role of each section.

Endlessly rewrite the prompt without fixing retrieval. Prompting cannot compensate for missing or wrong evidence indefinitely.
